## What landed

- **`procurement.py`** — four fail-closed extensions consumed by
  committed tenant data (ADR-208 §5): `exact_fields` on
  `[portal_where]` (per-term `upper(<field>) = '<TERM>'` equality
  clauses for identifier columns — WA DES's seven reviewed
  contract numbers `05720/02315/06316/04220/06913/00318/02702`
  surface reseller rows whose vendor name matches no vocabulary
  literal); `required_field`+`required_values` — a tenant's
  reviewed row-scope restriction folded server-side into every
  slice's `$where` AND enforced client-side at extract (the
  authoritative pass; a missing/empty/unlisted value counts
  `excluded` on the index row, never silently kept);
  `composite_id_fields` — the published row key joined verbatim
  (WA DES `contract_number|customer_name|vendor_name`) so a bare
  contract number never collapses distinct sales onto one
  subject; `rows_window = false` — a tenant whose reviewed
  surface IS the where filter expands no generic recency slice.
  P8-6 on portal sellers: a vendor/payee carrying the identity
  layer's affirmative `natural_person_signal` emits no `seller`
  claim, recorded `seller_dropped`; ambiguity refusals keep the
  text claim and merely mint no entity.
- **`dot_511.py`** — `aggregate_subject_kind` on the aggregate
  spec (closed vocabulary `camera_site` default |
  `programme_area`): a `programme_area` subject mints
  `programme_area:<source>:<target>:<key>` entity rows under the
  `programme_area` record kind and emits `programme_count`
  claims — never a `traffic_camera` subject or an
  `enforcement_count` claim. `aggregate_count_fields` (plural)
  beside `aggregate_count_field`: the transports emit one
  statistic/`$select` term per published measure column aliased
  `count_<field>`; each group row fans out into one
  `programme_count` claim per column with `series` naming the
  column verbatim. Multi-measure may not combine with `verbatim`
  count function or a discriminator; declaring both singular and
  plural forms is a registry error — all fail closed.
